published_source: Printed Table 3, Panel A, column (1) of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2021.01740.pdf, p. 7292; Panel B column (1) prints the same regression), read Nov 4 2026: Postlaunch 3.256*** (0.047), No. of products 5,742, Observations 101,803, R-squared 0.721, product FE and year-month FE; equals the authors' code output 3.256237 (0.0470163), N 101,803, to the printed decimals (authors_code_* hold the Stata/fixest re-run of do-file line 649, the same values as authors_rerun_twfe_raw). Earlier: tables/table3a.txt and tables/table3b.txt, column (1): post_event 3.256 (0.047), N = 101,803, R2 0.721
outcome: l_visits = log(1 + monthly page visits), SimilarWeb
replication_status: exact (authors' code output 3.256237 (0.0470163), N 101,803, equals printed Table 3 Panel A column (1) 3.256 (0.047), N 101,803, to the printed decimals; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
notes: reghdfe l_visits post_event, absorb(post_id year#month) cluster(post_id). fixest replication: 3.256237 (0.047016), N = 101,803, R2 0.7205: exact. Product-month panel built by ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2021.01740/prep.R from data/sample_regression_panel.dta with the do-file's Table 3/4 filters (drop femaleness_text_all4 missing; event_mo in [-6,12], event_mo != 0; 1 <= suggested_count <= 11 & ilink_created_at < newsletter_earliest (bytewise string comparison, as Stata) & is_in_newsletter == 0; post_id in data/in_sample_ids.dta): 103,356 rows, 5,742 products; 1,553 rows with missing l_visits drop -> 101,803. ym = year*12 + month (43 months Apr 2016 - Oct 2019 in the filtered panel; 41 with non-missing outcome, Jun 2016 - Oct 2019, since all missing-l_visits rows are pre-launch months in Apr-Jun 2016); launch_ym = post_year*12 + post_month (25 monthly launch cohorts, Oct 2016 - Oct 2018). Treatment onset is dated at the launch month (gvar = launch_ym), which the authors drop from the sample; on every kept row t >= launch_ym is identical to post_event (event_mo >= 1), so TWFE and BJS are unaffected, and the CSA base period g-1 is event month -1 (the paper's own event-study reference, ib5.time). With treat_var = post_event the cohort would be dated launch+1 and the CSA base period would be the dropped launch month, leaving no composition-fixed cells (same logic as the PROTOCOL 5b anticipation-bin rule). No never-treated products; each product is observed only in its own -6..+12 window (unbalanced in calendar time -> composition-fixed CSA cells). Columns 2-5 of the same table interact post_event with the product's femaleness score/quartiles or maker gender (subgroup-by-treatment interactions, excluded). Panels A and B share this column-1 regression; counted once. No article text or PDF available: published values are the authors' outreg2 output shipped in the package (tables/*.txt), which the README says was hand-formatted for publication. The launch effect is the baseline column, not the paper's headline gender-gap estimand (hence preferred = false, in_abstract_intro = false).
pipeline_caveat: No never-treated products and every product is observed only in its own -6..+12 window, so the linear component of the event-time profile is not separately identified from a calendar trend (rel = t - g with g absorbed by the unit FE). Pre-launch traffic ramps up steeply (raw mean l_visits 2.86 at event month -6, 5.23 at -1); the untreated-sample time FE absorb this ramp as a ~0.1 SD/month calendar trend, which BJS and CSA extrapolate into post-launch months. BJS by horizon falls from +0.53 SD (e=1) to -1.05 SD (e=12). CSA composition-fixed cells exist only for e = 1..4 (86 cells, 23 cohorts); BJS imputes 67.8% of treated rows (none after Sep 2018, when no untreated product is observed). See data/replication_logs/mnsc.2021.01740.md.
